You are on branch feature/WF03-ISS0881-20260929 (already checked out by the prior step; run `git branch --show-current` to confirm, and `git checkout feature/WF03-ISS0881-20260929` if not). Perform WF-03 Steps 0.5 (registry lookup) and 1 (diagnose) for docs/issues/ISS-0881.yaml in a single handoff, per docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md.

Step 0.5: read docs/issues/ISS-0873.yaml, ISS-0878.yaml, ISS-0879.yaml (all cited as precedent in ISS-0881.yaml's fix_direction field) in full. State in your result.summary whether ISS-0881's failure is the SAME root-cause mechanism as any of them (all three share a family resemblance -- platform-wide/unscoped reads racing a concurrent writer under scripts/test_parallel.sh contention -- but each has a distinct specific mechanism: ISS-0873 was a two-call bit-identical assertion racing a concurrent RetentionPolicy/Registration write; ISS-0879 was a throwaway test-support fixture row's visibility window leaking into an unscoped read; ISS-0878 was a process-local-only unique_integer collision across separate OS processes). Do not assume identity with any of them -- confirm or refute via your own investigation below.

Step 1: REPRODUCE the failure directly -- do not diagnose from ISS-0881.yaml's prose alone. Suggested approaches, in order of preference: (a) run the single failing test file repeatedly under real contention via `scripts/test_parallel.sh` (check its usage/flags first) or by running `mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs` concurrently alongside a separate full-suite background load (e.g. a second `mix test` process against the same Postgres instance) to recreate cross-partition contention against a single target test; (b) if true live reproduction proves impractical within reasonable time, high-confidence code-level analysis is acceptable PROVIDED you show your reasoning against the actual code paths involved (this is ISS-0873's own precedent, cited in ISS-0881.yaml's fix_direction, which reached resolution without live reproduction in that session -- but note ISS-0879's OWN resolution DID achieve isolated reproduction, so prefer that bar if you can reach it).

One lead worth checking, found during ORCH's own pre-dispatch read of the test file (verify or refute it yourself -- do not take it on faith, per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's 'a handoff's factual premises are checkable, and may be wrong' -- this is ORCH's own claim in this dispatch, so it is exactly such a premise): `sandbox_schema_names/0` (test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:571-582) queries `information_schema.schemata` for ALL schemas platform-wide matching `sandbox\_%`, unscoped to this test's own run -- the same class of unscoped global read ISS-0873/ISS-0879 diagnosed elsewhere. The failing assertion `refute MapSet.member?(final, o_schema)` (line 1126) checks a SPECIFIC schema name (`o_schema`, minted via `Ecto.UUID.generate()`-derived construction, lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex:930-933 -- effectively collision-proof across partitions), not the whole set, so a same-name collision from another partition is implausible; investigate instead whether `wait_until_schema_dropped(o_schema)` (called at line 1121, immediately before the failing assertion) can report success while a SUBSEQUENT `sandbox_schema_names()` call still observes the schema -- e.g. a connection-level snapshot/isolation effect (a connection checked out via `query_without_holding`/`retry_query_once` holding a transaction snapshot opened before the DROP SCHEMA committed), a retry-masking effect in `retry_query_once/1` hiding an actual failed drop, or a genuinely different mechanism you find in the actual code. Read `wait_until_schema_dropped/1`, `query_without_holding/1`, and `retry_query_once/1`'s definitions in full before concluding.

Do NOT implement a fix. Write the diagnosis into result.summary: root cause (not just symptom), the exact mechanism, affected files, and what a fix needs to change. Complete the handoff with next_action: 'Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design' (or, if your investigation finds no real defect / cannot be reproduced or root-caused with reasonable confidence after genuine effort, state that plainly and recommend the no_defect path instead -- do not force a fix design on a diagnosis you don't actually have).

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup, ISS-0873/ISS-0878/ISS-0879 read in full): all three share the family shape ISS-0881.yaml itself names (an assertion built on an unscoped, platform-wide Postgres read racing a concurrent writer in ANOTHER scripts/test_parallel.sh partition/OS-process), but each has a distinct concrete mechanism, and ISS-0881 is a FOURTH distinct mechanism in that same family, not a recurrence of any of the three: ISS-0873 = retention_summary/0's two-call bit-identical assertion racing a concurrent RetentionPolicy/Registration write; ISS-0878 = System.unique_integer/1 being only process-local unique, so two partitions' first calls with the same prefix produce a literal NAME collision on a global unique index; ISS-0879 = a throwaway tenant_template_build_* fixture row's migrations_applied_at visibility window leaking into provisioned_tenant_schemas/0. None of those three touch `sandbox_%` schemas or SandboxPool at all, so this is not a recurrence -- confirmed by reading each entry's mechanism, not assumed from the shared tag. Severity stays MINOR (no fix that 'didn't hold' to flag up).

STEP 1 (diagnose): ORCH's lead is CONFIRMED as the right code location but the wrong specific line -- verified, not taken on faith. Read wait_until_schema_dropped/1 (test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:176-198), query_without_holding/1 (:525-543), retry_query_once/1 (:555-565), schema_exists?/1 (:116-123) and sandbox_schema_names/0 (:571-582) in full, plus the production crash-handling path in lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex (handle_worker_death/1 :743-761, complete_op/3 :701-722) that RT-6 exercises. Findings:
  - schema_exists?/1 (used by wait_until_schema_dropped/1) is a SCOPED, single-row `WHERE schema_name = $1` query; DROP SCHEMA is transactional DDL taking ACCESS EXCLUSIVE, so once it commits it is immediately visible to every other connection under READ COMMITTED (Postgres has no dirty reads). This file also runs the whole module under Sandbox `:auto` mode (module moduledoc, confirmed at test file lines 9-35/52/60) specifically so every Repo call is a real, independent checkout/checkin -- there is no lingering transaction/snapshot on either the polling connection or the spawned-process connection sandbox_schema_names/0 uses via query_without_holding/1. So the 'stale snapshot on a held connection' hypothesis the dispatch handoff asked me to check is REFUTED for this module: it cannot explain a schema reappearing after wait_until_schema_dropped/1 reports it gone.
  - Checked the alternative hypothesis that the SandboxPool crash-handling path itself double-handles the killed worker and re-creates a schema of the same name after dropping it (which would be a real production defect, not just a test artifact): handle_worker_death/1's :provision clause enqueues exactly one {:drop, purpose: :orphan} op for o_schema and nothing re-provisions it; complete_op/3's {:drop, ...} clause only ever deletes the pool's own `active` bookkeeping entry. No re-creation path found. This hypothesis is REFUTED by direct code reading.
  - sandbox_schema_names/0 IS confirmed unscoped/platform-wide exactly as flagged: `SELECT schema_name FROM information_schema.schemata WHERE schema_name LIKE 'sandbox\_%'` with no filter tying it to this test's own pool instance or run. mint_sandbox_identity/0 (lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex:927-935) confirms o_schema is `"sandbox_" <> Ecto.UUID.generate()` with hyphens stripped -- a v4-UUID-derived name, collision-proof across partitions for all practical purposes. Grepped the whole tree for every consumer of SandboxPool.claim/release and found 8 OTHER test files beyond this one that create/drop real `sandbox_%` schemas via SandboxPool (either the shared application singleton pool config/test.exs configures, or their own pool instance): test/letflow/event_store/platform_events_test.exs, test/letflow/sandbox_pool/fixture_loader_test.exs, test/letflow/definitions/promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs, test/letflow/admission_test.exs, test/letflow/routers/req077_promotion_pipeline_test.exs, test/letflow/engine/plugin_registry_test.exs, test/letflow/sandbox_pool_call_timeout_test.exs, test/letflow/supervisor/infrastructure_test.exs.

ROOT CAUSE: under scripts/test_parallel.sh, ANY of those 8 other files running concurrently in a DIFFERENT OS-process/BEAM-VM partition against the same shared Postgres instance can create or drop its own real `sandbox_%` schema in the window between this test's `baseline = sandbox_schema_names()` (line 1091, captured before this test's own pool even starts) and its `final = sandbox_schema_names()` (line 1125) -- a window that spans this whole test's own claim+crash+drain+drop sequence. `sandbox_schema_names/0`'s unscoped read has no way to distinguish 'a schema this test's own pool created/dropped' from 'a schema some other partition's unrelated test created/dropped at the same wall-clock moment'. This is the exact same STRUCTURAL class as ISS-0873 (assertion built on an unscoped platform-wide read, implicitly assuming nothing else concurrently mutates that same state) but the fourth distinct concrete instance of it. The most likely failing assertion in practice is `assert final == baseline` (line 1127): it requires the ENTIRE platform-wide sandbox_% set to be bit-identical before and after, which any concurrent partition's own legitimate SandboxPool activity breaks by adding/removing an unrelated schema name.

DISCREPANCY FLAGGED (not a blocker, but worth CODE-DESIGNER/TEST-DESIGNER noting): ISS-0881.yaml's own description attributes the failure specifically to line 1126, `refute MapSet.member?(final, o_schema)`, not line 1127's `assert final == baseline`. Given o_schema is UUID-v4-derived (collision-proof), a same-NAME collision at line 1126 is not a plausible mechanism from anything found in this investigation -- I could not confirm which of the two adjacent assertions actually raised, because I was not able to reproduce the failure directly (see below) to capture a fresh stack trace, and no test/reports/ or handoffs/ artifact from the original discovering run (WF03-ISS0879-20260929) survived to cross-check against (handoffs/WF03-ISS0879-20260929/ is absent from this checkout and no matching test/reports/*.yaml entry was found). Root-cause fix should account for BOTH assertions being exposed to the same unscoped-read race (they read the same `final` snapshot), so this ambiguity does not change what needs fixing, but the exact line RELEASE-VALIDATOR transcribed may be an imprecise citation rather than the literal failing assertion -- flagging per 'a handoff's factual premises are checkable, and may be wrong' rather than silently overriding it.

REPRODUCTION ATTEMPT (real commands run, real output, did not reproduce): full scripts/test_parallel.sh (N up to 16 nproc-derived) was judged too costly to run blind here given it only reproduced 2 of 3 times even at full ~5000-test/16-partition scale in the original discovering session, so a single attempt at that scale is a low-information coin flip for the time cost on this host. Instead ran a smaller, targeted 2-OS-process contention rig modeled on test_parallel.sh's own per-partition MIX_BUILD_PATH isolation (separate _build/test-partA / _build/test-partB trees, `MIX_TEST_PARTITION=1` vs `2`, both against the same live Postgres instance): partition A looped `mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:1087` (targeting RT-6 directly); partition B looped the 8 other SandboxPool-consuming files identified above (first 3, then all 8 once found). Ran 18 total concurrent iterations across two configurations (8 iterations with 3 contending files, 10 iterations with all 8) -- zero failures, all iterations '1 passed, 22 excluded' / '116 passed' on both sides, no assertion failures, no exceptions. This is consistent with the mechanism being real but LOW-FREQUENCY -- it needs the much wider real-time window and far higher schema churn rate of a genuine full-suite run (thousands of tests, up to 16 concurrent partitions) to land inside the narrow gap between baseline/final on this one test, matching the issue's own '2 of 3 full runs' observed rate and MINOR severity, and matching ISS-0873's own explicit precedent (cited in this issue's fix_direction) of reaching a resolution via high-confidence code inspection without live in-session reproduction. Isolated single runs of the target test alone (`mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs`, 23/23 passed) and combined with all 8 other files sequentially (also all green) confirm no deterministic defect exists outside contention.

WHAT A FIX NEEDS TO CHANGE: sandbox_schema_names/0 (test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:571-582) needs to stop asserting on the platform-wide `sandbox_%` set as if this test were its only consumer. Candidate directions for CODE-DESIGNER to weigh (same shape as ISS-0873's own resolution, which reframed the test's assertion rather than changing production isolation, since SandboxPool's crash-handling logic itself was REFUTED as a source of the bug above): (a) scope the before/after comparison to only the schema name(s) this test's own pool instance actually minted (already known: o_schema, and any other schema_name a claim in this test returned) via a set-difference/subset assertion instead of `final == baseline` and `refute member` against the full platform-wide set -- e.g. assert `MapSet.difference(final, baseline)` contains nothing this test itself didn't already account for, rather than requiring the whole platform-wide set to be untouched; (b) if a genuinely bit-identical platform-wide guarantee is wanted, it would need every other SandboxPool-touching test file serialized against this one (impractical/against this suite's async design) so option (a) is the realistic direction. Affected files: test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs (the assertion logic and sandbox_schema_names/0's usage) only -- no production code in lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex needs to change, since the crash-handling path itself was checked and found correct.

issues.description: ISS-0881.yaml cites the failing assertion as sandbox_pool_test.exs:1126 (refute MapSet.member?(final, o_schema)), but o_schema is a v4-UUID-derived name that is collision-proof across partitions (lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex:927-935), making a same-name collision an implausible mechanism. The adjacent line 1127 (assert final == baseline) is structurally the far more plausible failure point under the unscoped-platform-wide-read race this diagnosis identifies. Could not confirm which line actually raised in the original run: no surviving handoffs/WF03-ISS0879-20260929/ artifact or matching test/reports/*.yaml entry to cross-check against, and this session's own reproduction attempts (18 iterations) did not reproduce the failure to capture a fresh trace. Flagged per core-directives.md's 'a handoff's factual premises are checkable, and may be wrong' -- does not change the recommended fix direction, since both assertions read the same unscoped `final` snapshot.

result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design: reframe sandbox_pool_test.exs's RT-6 (and any sibling case using the same sandbox_schema_names()-based before/after pattern) to assert only against schemas this test's own pool instance is responsible for, rather than the full unscoped platform-wide sandbox_% set, per result.summary's 'what a fix needs to change' section. No production code change indicated in lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex.
